title: ZIdentity resource servers (API resources): a read-only registry of the scopes API clients can select

prose.text: Resource servers are what the console calls API resources: the scopes an API client can be given. {{definition}}

prose.label: The record.
prose.text: {{record-required}} {{primary-aud-and-default-api}} What `defaultApi` changes is open {{gap:default-api-behavior}}, as is what a resource server with no service scopes means {{gap:empty-service-scopes}}.

prose.label: Services inside a record.
prose.text: {{service-cloud-org-required}} The Go SDK has seen services without those two fields {{divergence:service-cloud-org}}. {{go-extra-service-fields}} {{extra-fields-not-in-contract}}

prose.label: Linking to API clients.
prose.text: {{clients-reference-resources}} {{no-back-reference}} The scope IDs are passed to the client unchanged: [[zidentity.api-clients:scope-id-composite]].

prose.label: Listing them.
prose.text: Lists page like every ZIdentity list: [[zidentity.api.pagination]]. Whether the list shows every resource server or hides internal ones is open {{gap:enumerability}}. Go's name lookup filters on the client: [[zidentity.sdk-go:getbyname-client-side]]. Python's get method is annotated loosely: [[zidentity.sdk-python:annotation-mismatches]].

checks.do: For a resource or scope missing when building an API client, whether the product is linked to Authentication Service and has an API role, since resources are created from those roles.
Which API clients use a resource server, by reading the clients' `clientResources`, since the resource server lists none.
Whether code reading a service's `cloudName` or `orgName` tolerates them being absent for the ZIdentity and Z-Insights services.

definition.statement: API resources are the Zscaler APIs available through the OneAPI gateway: collections of Zscaler API endpoints representing data entities, services or functions that API clients can access.

quotes: API resources refer to the Zscaler APIs available via the OneAPI gateway.
The API resources are a collection of Zscaler API endpoints that represent various data entities, services, or functionalities that can be accessed by the API clients.

auto-created.statement: API resources are created automatically, based on the RBAC roles applicable to the APIs within the various Zscaler services.

quotes: The API resources are automatically created in the Zscaler Admin Console based on the role-based access control (RBAC) roles applicable to the APIs within the various Zscaler services.

linked-services.statement: API resources exist for the Zscaler services linked to Authentication Service, and an API client can access the API resources of those linked services.

quotes: The API resources are available for the Zscaler services (Internet & SaaS, Private Access, Zscaler Client Connector, etc.) that are linked to Authentication Service and the API client can access the API resources of the linked Zscaler services.

scopes-no-write-path.statement: The contract has no operation to create, change or delete a resource server's scopes either.
scopes-no-write-path.conditions: Rests on a search of every path in zid.openapi.json: the only paths naming resource servers or scopes are /resource-servers and /resource-servers/{id}, both GET-only; no scope path exists to check directly.

read-only.statement: The contract offers only GET on the resource server collection and on a single resource server: neither path has an operation to create, change or delete a resource server.

record-required.statement: A resource server record carries `id`, `name`, `displayName`, `description`, `primaryAud`, `defaultApi` and `serviceScopes`, all marked required; each service scope pairs a `service` with its `scopes`.

primary-aud-and-default-api.statement: The contract describes `primaryAud` as the resource server's primary audience, and `defaultApi` only as whether the resource server is set as the default API.

expect.description: The primary audience of the resource server, identifying the primary entity or context for which the server is intended.
Whether this resource server is set as the default API.

service-cloud-org-required.statement: The contract marks a service's `cloudName` (the cloud hosting it) and `orgName` (the organization associated with it) as required.

go-extra-service-fields.statement: The Go SDK's service model also carries `externalName`, which has matched `name` in every response its authors observed, and `zapsOnboarded`, which is undocumented and was observed false for every service on the tenants examined.

quotes: ExternalName is the service's stable programmatic name. It has matched
Name in every response observed, but the API reports both, so both are
ZapsOnboarded is undocumented and has been observed as false for every

extra-fields-not-in-contract.statement: Neither `externalName` nor `zapsOnboarded` is in the contract's service schema, and the Python service model reads only `id`, `name`, `displayName`, `cloudName` and `orgName`.

quotes: self.id = config["id"] if "id" in config else None
self.name = config["name"] if "name" in config else None
self.display_name = config["displayName"] if "displayName" in config else None
self.cloud_name = config["cloudName"] if "cloudName" in config else None

extra-fields-not-in-contract.conditions: The five reads quoted are every field the Python Service model reads at the pin.

clients-reference-resources.statement: An API client's `clientResources` lists the resource servers it may reach and the scopes selected on each; the Go SDK says to resolve those resource and scope IDs with its resource servers package.

quotes: ClientResources is required, and lists the resource servers the client may
reach along with the scopes selected for each. Resolve the resource and
scope ids with the resource_servers package.

no-back-reference.statement: A resource server record does not list the API clients that use it, so finding them means reading each client's `clientResources`.
no-back-reference.conditions: The record's required list is also its complete property list in the contract at the pin; no client field appears.

service-cloud-org.summary: The contract requires `cloudName` and `orgName` on every service in a resource server, while the Go SDK records that services that are not cloud-scoped, ZIAM and ZINSIGHTS, come without either.

quotes: CloudName and OrgName are absent for services that are not cloud-scoped —
ZIAM and ZINSIGHTS are reported without either.

positions.says: The ZIAM and ZINSIGHTS services carry neither field.

service-cloud-org.impact: A strict client generated from the contract can fail to decode a resource server that includes the ZIdentity or Z-Insights service; treat both fields as optional.

default-api-behavior.title: What a resource server's `defaultApi` flag changes
default-api-behavior.detail: Unverified legacy statement: when `defaultApi` is true the resource server is implicitly available. The contract says only that it marks the resource server as the default API, and the client-side `defaultApi` on `clientResources` is reported on read only; no source says which clients it applies to or what it overrides.
default-api-behavior.blocks: explaining why a client reaches a resource it was not given explicitly

empty-service-scopes.title: What a resource server with an empty `serviceScopes` list means
empty-service-scopes.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the meaning of an empty `serviceScopes` (no scopes available, all scopes, or scopes defined elsewhere) is undocumented. The contract requires the field but not that it be non-empty.
empty-service-scopes.blocks: building an API client from a resource server that lists no scopes

enumerability.title: Whether listing resource servers returns all of them, or hides Zscaler-internal ones
enumerability.detail: Unverified legacy statement: whether `list_resource_servers` returns all resource servers including Zscaler-internal ones, or only tenant-visible ones, is unconfirmed. The list operation has no parameter separating system-provided from other entries, and no capture compares its output with the console's API Resources page.
enumerability.blocks: treating the API's list as the full set of selectable resources
